Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Hollow-frame interior recoloring

Use when multiple hollow monochrome rectangular outlines appear on a uniform background and demos recolor their interiors.

## When to Use
Load this skill when ARC grids contain hollow rectangular frames with possible interior fill/recoloring. Treat all specific mappings as task-specific evidence, not universal laws.

## Evidence from validated Continual-ARC examples
Multiple demos show all complete rectangular outlines filled uniformly, including interiors whose cells initially contain a different color; those markers are overwritten. In one three-demo task, observed strict-interior dimensions and output colors included: 1x1→7; 2x2→2; 3x3→7; 2x3→7; 4x4→2; 4x5→7; and 5x5→7. This supports the task-specific selector “square interior with even side length gets 2; otherwise gets 7.” Distinct outline colors can share a fill color, and one outline color can yield different fills at different dimensions, so the border color is not the selector. Another previously recorded example likewise suggested 2x2→2 and several odd/non-square sizes→7.

Use this as a hypothesis template, not a universal law: re-derive both the palette mapping and dimension selector from current demos. A particularly easy-to-miss case is a 3x3 outline (1x1 interior): the test in task-56e3e7ed had two such frames and both interiors became 7, not the even-square fill color 2.

## Workflow
1. Identify complete hollow rectangular outlines; record each bounding box and verify all four sides are continuous.
2. Determine the strict interior dimensions (height−2, width−2), excluding outline cells.
3. Compare every interior cell in input/output, including cells initially non-background. Check whether interiors are uniformly overwritten and whether incomplete/nonrectangular objects remain unchanged.
4. Infer the fill-color selector from demos. Distinguish object palette, interior dimensions/area, and original interior contents; test competing rules against every frame.
5. Apply the validated rule to all detected frames, overwriting interior cells if demos support it and preserving outlines/background elsewhere.
6. Validate grid dimensions and row widths mechanically before submission.

## Pitfalls
- Do not only recolor interior cells that match the background: the demos may show existing singleton markers overwritten as well.
- Do not infer fill color from border color alone when same-color frames of different dimensions behave differently.
- A wrong full-grid submission invalidates the hypothesis; revisit both missed frames and selector logic.
